analysis_steps.goal: Process and image ALMA continuum and spectral line data

method.value: Calibrated data reduced in CASA; continuum imaged across line-free ranges in LSB and USB (249.30-253.05 GHz and 264.96-268.71 GHz); spectral cube rebinned to 166 MHz (200 km s^-1) channels.

evidence.quote: We rebin our data to a resolution of 166 MHz (200 km s^-1)... We averaged fluxes over the two spectral windows of LSB (249.30-253.05 GHz or 1.203-1.185mm) and USB (264.96-268.71 GHz or 1.131-1.116mm) in the range of frequency free from the [C II] line.

key_parameters.value: Rebinned resolution: 166 MHz (200 km s^-1); continuum effective frequency: 259.01 GHz

evidence.quote: We rebin our data to a resolution of 166 MHz (200 km s^-1)... Figure 1 presents the resulting ALMA continuum data at 259.01 GHz in frequency (or 1.167mm in wavelength) with a 1sigma sensitivity of 17.4uJy beam^-1.

validation.value: Compared apparent 2-sigma peak at target position with surrounding negative noise peaks at 2-3 sigma level to establish non-detection.

evidence.quote: There is a ~ 2sigma flux peak in the beam size on the position of Himiko. However, there are a series of negative pixels nearby that correspond to the 2-3 sigma level per beam. We conclude therefore that Himiko remains undetected

analysis_steps.goal: Derive FIR continuum luminosity upper limit

method.value: Derived 3-sigma upper limit on L_FIR by integrating an optically thin graybody modified blackbody model from 8 to 1000 um.

evidence.quote: Assuming an optically thin graybody of modified blackbody radiation with a dust emissivity power-law spectral index of beta_d=1.5 and a dust temperature of T_d=40K (Eales et al. 1989; Klaas et al. 1997), we obtain a 3sigma upper limit of L_FIR < 8.0 x 10^10 L_odot integrated over 8-1000um.

key_parameters.value: beta_d = 1.5, T_d = 40 K (also explored T_d = 20-60 K, beta_d = 0-2)

evidence.quote: Assuming an optically thin graybody of modified blackbody radiation with a dust emissivity power-law spectral index of beta_d=1.5 and a dust temperature of T_d=40K

assumptions.value: Optically thin dust emission; local thermal equilibrium between ISM and CMB at z=6.595 imposes T_d >= 21 K.

evidence.quote: Assuming local thermal equilibrium between ISM of Himiko and CMB at z=6.595 (da Cunha et al. 2013), this yields a lower limit of T_d=21 K.

validation.value: Checked sensitivity to alternative T_d (25 K, 60 K) and beta_d (0, 2) values.

evidence.quote: For T_d=25K and T_d=60K, the 3sigma upper limit luminosities in 8-1000um are <2.7 x 10^10 and <3.0 x 10^11 L_odot, respectively. Similarly, for beta_d=0 and beta_d=2, the 3sigma upper limit luminosities in 8-1000um are <3.5 x 10^10 and <1.2 x 10^11 L_odot

method.value: Searched velocity channels within +-600 km s^-1 around z_Lya=6.595; derived 3-sigma line flux and luminosity upper limit and compared to De Looze et al. (2011) relation.

evidence.quote: The corresponding 3sigma upper limit for [C II] is 250.0 uJy in a channel width of 200 km s^-1. The associated luminosity limit is <5.4 x 10^7 L_odot.
Himiko clearly departs significantly from the scaling relation; the deficit amounts to a factor ~ x30.

evidence.quote: We searched for a signal of [C II] over 600 km s^-1 around the frequency corresponding to z_Lya=6.595.

evidence.quote: The line sensitivity is defined with a channel width of 200 km s^-1.

validation.value: Verified non-detection across velocity range and identified that ~3 sigma peaks slightly offset from optical center are noise peaks.

evidence.quote: there are noise peaks barely reaching at the 3sigma level in 0 km s^-1 and -200 km s^-1 that are slightly north and south of the Himiko’s optical center position, respectively. However, neither of these sources is a reliable counterpart of Himiko.

findings_qualitative.value: Himiko is undetected in 1.2 mm dust continuum (<52 uJy) and [C II] 158 um emission (<250 uJy), indicating dust-poor and metal-poor interstellar gas.

evidence.quote: Both aspects of our ALMA observations suggest Himiko is an unique object with a very low dust content and perhaps nearly primordial interstellar gas.

findings_qualitative.value: Himiko falls below the local [C II]-SFR relation by a factor of >30, implying gas-phase metallicity <= 0.03 Z_sun.

evidence.quote: our observations indicate Himiko lies off the local L_[CII] - star formation rate scaling relation by a factor of more than 30.

evidence.loc: 4.1 The Low Dust and Metal Content of Himiko
evidence.quote: De Looze (2012) has argued that offsets from the [C II]-SFR relation can be explained in terms of metal abundance and this would imply a gas-phase metallicity of <~ 0.03Z_odot.

findings_qualitative.value: HST imaging reveals Himiko consists of three distinct L* clumps undergoing a triple major merger.

evidence.quote: Himiko is undergoing a triple major merger event whose extensive ionized nebula of Lyman alpha emitting gas, discovered in our earlier work with Subaru, is powered by star formation and the dense circum-galactic gas.

claims.hypothesis: Himiko contains cold dust emission and significant obscured star formation traceable by ALMA 1.2 mm continuum.
claims.experiment: Conducted deep ALMA Band 6 continuum imaging targeting 1.2 mm (259 GHz) with 17.4 uJy beam^-1 rms sensitivity.
claims.result: No dust continuum detected, placing a 3-sigma upper limit of <52.1 uJy (L_FIR < 8.0 x 10^10 L_sun).
claims.finding: Himiko has very low dust content, with SFR(FIR) < 14 M_sun yr^-1, ruling out substantial obscured star formation.

evidence.loc: 4.1 The Low Dust and Metal Content of Himiko
evidence.quote: we obtain SFR(FIR) < 14 M_odot yr^-1 that is far smaller than not only our best optical-NIR estimate SFR of ~ 100 M_odot yr^-1, but also the UV-luminosity SFR of SFR(UV)=30 +- 2 M_odot yr^-1 with no dust extinction correction.

claims.hypothesis: The [C II] 158 um line traces star formation in Himiko following the local [C II]-SFR scaling relation.
claims.experiment: Targeted redshifted [C II] at 250.24 GHz with ALMA Band 6 down to 83.3 uJy beam^-1 per 200 km s^-1 channel.
claims.result: No line detected; 3-sigma upper limit L_[CII] < 5.4 x 10^7 L_sun.
claims.finding: Himiko departs from the local [C II]-SFR relation by a factor of >30, indicating very low metallicity (<=0.03 Z_sun) and/or high PDR density.

evidence.quote: Himiko clearly departs significantly from the scaling relation; the deficit amounts to a factor ~ x30.

claims.hypothesis: Himiko's extensive Ly-alpha halo and extreme star formation are caused by gravitational lensing or an active galactic nucleus.
claims.experiment: Examined high-resolution HST/WFC3 imaging, deep Spitzer/IRAC imaging, X-ray limits, and existing Keck spectroscopy.
claims.result: HST resolves three distinct L* clumps with asymmetric properties; no foreground lens, no X-ray detection, and no high-ionization emission lines.
claims.finding: Gravitational lensing and AGN excitation are ruled out; Himiko is an unlensed triple major merger powered by starburst photoionization.

evidence.quote: Thus, we conclude that Himiko is not a gravitational lensed system... Thus, we conclude the Lya halo is unlikely to be heated by an active galactic nucleus.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Band 6 reaches an order of magnitude deeper than previous IRAM observations, capable of detecting dust continuum and [C II] 158 um to test for obscured star formation and metallicity.

evidence.quote: Our ALMA observations probe an order of magnitude deeper than previous IRAM observations, yet fail to detect a 1.2mm dust continuum

why_this_method.value: Combining ALMA with HST WFC3 and Spitzer SEDS allows simultaneous morphological deconstruction into subcomponents and multi-wavelength SED modeling.

evidence.quote: The present paper is concerned with the analysis of uniquely deep ALMA and HST observations of this remarkable source.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Considered and rejected gravitational lensing, central AGN heating, single virialized galaxy with HII clumps, and strong shock-driven outflows as explanations for Himiko.

evidence.quote: we conclude that Himiko is not a gravitational lensed system... we conclude the Lya halo is unlikely to be heated by an active galactic nucleus... we consider that Himiko is unlikely to be a single virialized system

limitations_admitted.value: Far-infrared luminosity and dust mass upper limits depend strongly on assumed dust temperature T_d and emissivity index beta_d.

evidence.quote: Note that these upper limits depend upon the assumed dust temperature and beta_d. For T_d=25K and T_d=60K, the 3sigma upper limit luminosities in 8-1000um are <2.7 x 10^10 and <3.0 x 10^11 L_odot, respectively.

limitations_admitted.value: HST F098M detects only marginal extended Ly-alpha emission due to the shallower surface brightness limit of HST compared to Subaru.

evidence.quote: The F098M image in Figure 4 detects only marginal extended Lya emission, because of the shallower surface brightness limit of the 2.4m HST compared to the 8m Subaru telescope.

referee_caveats_inferred: The severe deficit in [C II] emission relative to SFR could alternatively be caused by [C II] deficit at high FIR surface brightness or collisional de-excitation in high-density PDRs rather than solely low metallicity.
Derivation of SFR from UV/optical SED fitting is sensitive to assumptions about SFH and nebular line contributions.

reproducibility.score_reason: The paper provides clear project codes, observing details, sensitivities, upper limits, and SED modeling assumptions. However, imaging parameters (weighting/robust, pixel cell size) in CASA and details of the SED fitting software scripts are not completely documented.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Early Science data (2011.0.00115.S) with clear null detection result (<52.1 uJy continuum, <250 uJy line) that is straightforward to re-image and verify.
